rules.assurance: A recognized source pattern is a review signal, not proof of reachable exploitation, complete data flow, runtime protection or an acceptance-check pass.
rules.description: A system or developer message contains an obvious external-input expression. Untrusted data may be interpreted as privileged instructions; local analysis cannot establish exploitability.

implementation_guidance.agent_mcp_relevance: External text inserted into a system/developer message is promoted into the same channel as trusted agent policy. A retrieved document or tool response may then steer planning and sensitive tool arguments.
applicability: Trace whether the interpolated value is actually external, configuration-owned or a deliberately trusted instruction; this local pattern does not prove a successful prompt injection.
Moving content to a lower-trust message reduces instruction confusion but does not guarantee the model will ignore adversarial content.
residual_risk: Delimiters, provenance labels and system prompts are not complete injection defenses; model behavior and workflow composition require ongoing tests.
